subject: Pricing follow-up: token economics and benchmarking (Redwood vs OpenAI/Anthropic)

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Pricing follow-up: token economics and benchmarking (Redwood vs OpenAI/Anthropic)

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the next steps we discussed: 

- Use case: conversational customer support + short summarization for support tickets.
- Expected volumes: peak ~50M tokens/month, steady-state ~12M tokens/month.
- Latency SLO: 200-300ms p95 for 1-2k concurrent users.
- Data requirements: SOC2 + optional VPC private deployment later.

Action items we agreed:
1) I’ll send a short pricing note with unit economics and benchmarking vs common hosts.
2) Acme to confirm committed volume range and target $/1M tokens for procurement.
3) If numbers look good, we’ll send a one-page proposal and SOW for procurement to review.

Below are two practical pricing scenarios (ballpark) to help you evaluate unit economics today - these are meant to be discussion starters, not a formal quote:

Option A - Pay-as-you-go (no commit):
- Redwood (managed hosted, standard LLM): $20 / 1M tokens (list)
- OpenAI (comparable model): $28 / 1M tokens (public pricing proxy)
- Anthropic (comparable model): $30 / 1M tokens
- Other open-model hosts (self-hosted or lower-cost hosts): $10-18 / 1M tokens (varies by infra/latency)

Option B - Committed monthly reservation (6-12mo):
- Redwood: $9-12 / 1M tokens (tiered based on commit) - typical target we’ve seen for customers at ~10-50M/mo
- OpenAI: effectively higher on comparable commitments in many cases due to model mix

Notes on assumptions:
- Numbers assume a production-ready model variant (quantized if applicable) with 1-2 token-generation multiplier for prompt+response.
- We include automatic batching/prefix caching benefits in the committed price band.
- We can structure a 3-month pilot with a short-term credit to validate production economics; if pilot volume hits thresholds we convert to a committed band.

Next steps: I’ll attach a short proposal and SOW for procurement. Can you confirm the target price band Acme is evaluating (e.g., target $/1M tokens) and the procurement timeline?

Thanks -
Vanessa Ortiz

Sarah -

Great - those volume and budget ranges are helpful. Short answers up front: yes, we can structure committed pricing in the $9-12 / 1M tokens band for the steady-state volumes you described, depending on term and minimum monthly commit. Details below.

Committed pricing (example tiers):
- 6mo commit, 10M tokens/mo guaranteed: $12 / 1M tokens
- 12mo commit, 10M tokens/mo guaranteed: $10 / 1M tokens
- 12mo commit, 25M tokens/mo guaranteed: $9 / 1M tokens

Pilot recommendation:
- 3-month pilot (no long-term lock), capped PO for up to 10M tokens in month 1 and 12M in month 2-3. We offer a one-time onboarding credit that offsets ~30-40% of pilot consumption to validate QoE and ops integration. If you convert to a 12mo commit within 30 days of pilot completion we can apply that credit to the first invoice.

Benchmark context (how Redwood compares in practice):
- OpenAI/Anthropic: public model endpoints tend to be higher cost per 1M tokens for comparable latency/managed endpoints - often 20-40% higher list pricing for similar model families.
- Other open-model hosts/self-managed: raw infra costs can be lower, but you trade off management, SLOs, and integrated caching/batching that Redwood provides; effective production cost often ends up similar once those are included.

I attached a one-page proposal and a draft SOW for procurement review (redwood_price_proposal_v1.pdf, SOW-Acme-Redwood-2026.docx). Procurement can use the SOW as a starting point; let me know preferred PO or DocuSign routing and we’ll surface a formal quote.

If $10-12 / 1M is the procurement target, I recommend the 12mo 10M tier to start - it hits $10 and gives you room to burst/scale with committed pricing protections.

Would you like us to prepare a formal quote (DocuSign) for the 12mo / 10M tier?

Best -
